utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll start in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I return your attention to the question of Lord Ashdown's evidence and add to what I was able to reveal to you yesterday about the existence of the statement of Lord Ashdown by informing you or re-informing you that indeed a video has been taken from the positions that Lord Ashdown gives as the coordinates of where he was. And although that video has yet to be provided to the other parties, simply for want of time, it only having come into the office last week and needing to be processed, it is a potentially extremely valuable piece of material to resolve this issue, without, for example, obliging people either to do more work on the issue or go to the region to check it out themselves. Now, the complex position in which we find ourselves is not of the Prosecution's making. It is entirely as a result of the approach taken by the accused through this witness. The evidential position developing from Lord Ashdown saying roughly where he was and what he saw, through attempts by the Defence evidence to say that this was impossible and something he couldn't see, now apparently to attempts to rely on what's said to be expert material, which is going to be added to, we know, by further maps that the witness is going to have drawn overnight. I have not yet been in a position to serve the statement that accompanies the video, and therefore perhaps one of the reasons the video hasn't yet itself gone. I suppose I might be in a position next week, if given leave to cross-examine again on the basis of the video and to put the video to the witness and so on. But the position is becoming complex and consuming of time on a topic that is -- should be, in our submission, comparatively straightforward. And it's becoming complex probably, or possibly, because material is being placed before you that is not helpful and may even be misleading. So that, for example, we still cannot understand, in respect of the maps provided, why the sight-line positions have been chosen, because none of them seem to relate to the evidence given by Lord Ashdown. How we should proceed from here is a little hard to know. I had the statement and the video been available in advance, I probably would have wanted it served on the accused and on the witness, in the hope that this might bring him to a realisation that what Lord Ashdown said about his ability to see things is accurate and true, because the witness hasn't been to these positions himself, he's only working it from other material. We're not able to do that, and I'm frankly not quite sure where we should proceed from here. What I would press the Chamber at this stage is to be cautious or conservative in the leave it gives to this witness at this stage to start speculating or to work on the expert or so-called expert material of others. But I can only invite the Chamber to take that position if, as I explained, there is rebuttal evidence available not only in the form of Lord Ashdown's statement but in the form of a video, and it's a video that, if I can, I may serve on the other parties today, with or without the statement that explains it. The video has a soundtrack of the investigator saying what he's looking at, so it to some degree is complete and self-sufficient. And it lasts -- but it's about 20 minutes of text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You would be seeking to put that video in evidence at what stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Rebuttal would be the standard place to put it in in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There might be an argument here, I put it no higher than that, that there ought to be further cross-examination in a situation where it was never put to Ashdown in his evidence when he was here that he couldn't see what he claimed to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I absolutely accept that. Lord Ashdown is willing to come back. But in the management of the trial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no. I don't mean that. I mean that further -- another opportunity might be given to you to cross-examine this witness following the re-examination and in the light of the reaction you get to the video. I wasn't thinking as far ahead as Lord Ashdown giving evidence again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'd be grateful for that. I am aware of the time this issue is consuming for the procedural reasons I've already explained. There it is. That's the information I can give you. I'm not yet in a position to deal with the Atlantic Brigade. I'll come back to you as soon as I am. But I have so far not received response from those whom I have sought assistance from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear from Mr. Nice when that video footage that he intends to serve was actually filmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It was filmed this summer, in response to the evidence of this -- effectively in response to the evidence of this witness. And to my knowledge, none of the hills that are to be seen in the video at the present have been formed since the time when Lord Ashdown gave his evidence first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I suppose not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have one more thing to say, Mr. Robinson. Does that mean that the cameraman went there to the region without Lord Ashdown to establish what could possibly be seen from various points, or did he go to the exact spot where Lord Ashdown said in his testimony he was located at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're not dealing with the video now, questions of admissibility, so you don't need to get into those questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. One more matter. It was said that the witness has not been there, so he could not possibly know. That is only partially true. The units subordinate to the witness were there, and it was their job to be on the border. And they had the assignment to observe the border line and the border belt. So it is not completely correct to say that the witness cannot know because he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me give the Trial Chamber's decision in relation to some exhibits. Delic exhibits, I'll deal first with tabs from Exhibit D300. We'll admit tab 104, 111, 125, 136, 148, 149, and 342. Other documents now. The Serb version of the Split clips 1, 3, 4, 8, and 9, 11, 13, 15, also Pavkovic's order, the picture of the woman and daughter in video clip in tab 476. The video of the interview with the woman interviewed in tab 476. The statement of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The statement of Lulzim Kolgjeraj; statement of Mihill Bezhi, statement of Llesh Lekaj, the war diary, the video clip from the BBC showing pictures of refugees in Macedonia; Noam Chomsky book, The New Humanistic Militarism, page 30. And then in relation to Mr. Seselj, D303, tab 9; D303, tab 11; D303, tab 29; D303, tabs 9 and 11. And I'm to say that tab - sorry - that D309 consists of seven tabs, not six, as was indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to note that those exhibits refer to -- in relation to Delic are those used by the Prosecution, and the new exhibits should be given numbers in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, it was my understanding that the exhibits of General Delic from the time when he went through his examination-in-chief were admitted. So now we're talking about something different, aren't we? If we are, then I ask that General Clark's book be admitted into evidence as well, the one that General Delic quoted yesterday. He marked the page, he gave an exact reference. And that is very important evidence. It shows the alliance, or rather, the concerted action between NATO and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted, page -- what was the page? We'll get the page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be found in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: General Clark's book was only admitted in passages, I believe, not in whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only those passages referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And we'll probably need an English page reference. I think the witness was reading from a B/C/S page reference yesterday. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll check it and have the corresponding reference for the English pagination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say that there's a difference between the Serb pagination and the English pagination, the pages are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we're aware of that. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I now move on to those questions that you've postponed until today, that is to say maps, and 3-D photographs, the ones I handed out to everyone yesterday through the liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, you may.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday I gave you some maps, or rather, 3-D photographs of parts of the terrain that Mr. Ashdown testified about. I put some questions to you about that during the examination-in-chief. You challenged what he had said, as you presented material facts in this regard. Could you please place on the ELMO and briefly explain the map marked number 1. A pencil was used to mark the maps, and I hope that you had the opportunity of having a look at them. Could you please explain what this map represents, and particularly, whether it represents the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. terrain that Mr. Ashdown referred to during his testimony.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a three-dimensional picture, and it was probably made on the basis of Lord Ashdown's --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Probably made. He doesn't know anything about this document. This is somebody else's material, not even accompanied by a statement explaining what it is, handed to a witness, and you're going to be asked to draw some assistance from his comments on it. This line of re-examination should, in my respectful submission, be curtailed and move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I think that it has to do with imprecision in the witness's speech, knowing the terrain and knowing the map. The witness could have said that it was undoubtedly done in that terrain rather than probably. Since the witness is so familiar with the terrain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have had a look at all the images, and what Mr. Nice said just now, this can be explained by any officer. I think that Mr. Nice's objection is out of order. So this is part of the border that is the highest peak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, it's not for a witness to start claiming that anyone's objection is out of order. I have not had it explained to me yet what this is. I have no idea what it is. I do understand what the maps are that follow, but the first document is meaningless at the moment to me, and I don't know the basis of the witness's knowledge about what it is, or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, can you establish the basis of the witness's knowledge in relation to this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, can you recognise the terrain that is depicted in this image, and what does this 3-D image represent?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully recognise the terrain. This is a 3-D image that was made on the basis of vectors on a computer. And it has to do with the terrain of Morina, Gegaj, Kamenica, and the immediate state border between Yugoslavia and Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How is it you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be seen here. You can read it here on the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, you read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying there's something written on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Can you see this here? Can you see what I'm showing now? It says "Maja Glava." Can you see that it says "Kamenica" here, that that's what's written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're recognising this terrain from what's written on the map; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm recognising this terrain according to what it looks like and according to what the map says. I was in the area dozens of times. And you see it says Gegaj here. That's what's written here. Can you see the colouring here, the state border?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is a terrain which undoubtedly includes the village of Gegaj and the entire configuration surrounding it, including the state border that is marked here.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just tell you where Junik is, because that was in dispute. Junik is behind this elevation here, behind it. Several hundred metres lower down, behind this. That is why I said that the lord could see Junik only if he could see through a hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where did you say Gegaj is? Could you point the place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]. You can even read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I hope that you've all received copies. I've given a sufficient number of sets of these maps, gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where is Batusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Batusa cannot be seen. Batusa cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Bucaj, Bucaj in Albania?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Albania? As far as Albania is concerned, you can see that the area includes the immediate surroundings of Gegaj, and Kamenica, and this part of the border, and it doesn't go further into the Albanian territory. So this 3-D image was made as one views the terrain from Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this is viewed from where in Albania? Where's the viewpoint? Do you know where is the viewpoint of this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll have to take my own map. This is viewed from trig point 805, towards Gegaj and the area that looks towards Brovina Kodra, trig point 805. It's the direction from Albania. And that's the viewpoint for this 3-D image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it not look to you as if it was viewed from mid-air and not from the ground at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gentlemen, I would not like to go into explanations now as to how 3-D imagery is made. It is made on the basis of existing maps. Then vector values of altitude are entered, and then the computer makes this kind of image. You can get this kind of image for any part of my territory. That is why you see that these names, Maja Glava, Gegaj, Kamenica, are different, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you not get the image, though, from a particular point, in other words, a point on the ground, as if you were viewing it from that point? And if you do, why can't we just be told how it was done rather than leave you to speculate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not guessing at all. I'm not speculating. This is my own line of work. But how can I explain it to you? How can I explain vector values to you, on the basis of which maps are drawn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're saying that the trig point you've given as 805 is the point where the feet of the person who would have this view would be located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When this image was made, this 3-D image, the wish was to show Kamenica, Gegaj, and the direction that Lord Ashdown said he saw in Kosovo and Metohija. That was the objective, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question, which is whether the trig point you've identified, 805, is where the feet would be of the person who would see this image, looking out across country. Or is that not what it would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you not answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, your question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm assuming Lord Ashdown's feet were on the ground when he viewed. Now, are we seeing the equivalent of a picture, a person with his feet on the ground would take from trig point 805, or are we not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This image shows only that if Lord Ashdown is standing near the state border, near the village of Gegaj, that he cannot see Junik. This image was made only for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm curious, of course, that it should be made for that purpose, given that Lord Ashdown didn't claim to see Junik, but claimed to see areas south of Junik. And unfortunate that our time should be being taken when I think the accused is substantially through the amount of time allowed for his case, 60 per cent or something like that, and we're taking time on issues like this. I really must press the Chamber to bring this to a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we're dealing with truth, Mr. Nice, that means that Lord Ashdown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You are not to comment -- don't comment on the truthfulness of any witness. That's not your province. Mr. Milosevic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, would you now place on the ELMO and give us your comments of the number 2 picture, entitled "Cross Relief on the Gegaj-Junik Axis."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map, a picture, topographical map, in fact, showing the axis, the direction, from trig 804 towards trigometric point around Junik. And what we see down at the bottom is the graph relief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clear this up, General. According to the trig point south of Junik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's it. So the relief graph, in red, shows --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you put it up a bit? Because we can't see it on the ELMO. May we see the graph at the bottom of the reliefs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The red shows what you cannot see. The computer here should have introduced a green line here. So what is lacking here is the green colour, the green line, and that is what can be seen from that particular point. And it refers to this direction and axis. The visibility is only from this point to that, and this small portion there. All the red line shows the configuration of the terrain and the impossibility of seeing anything along this axis, anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what do we see on the right-hand side of the line, the visibility line?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A point south of Junik and the distance to that point, which is 9.492 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I hope that that is clear now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have on the ELMO another map now, please. It is map number 3, the binocular view and cross-section of the relief along the Gegaj-Junik axis.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this point here is around Gegaj and it shows the area south of Junik, across Batusa, a point there, a point which in fact is located in the Junik stream. And on the graph, you can see the green line, the green curve, which shows that portion which is visible from the point, and the red curves indicate the points that aren't visible. It is 7.480 metres -- 408 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So those lines denote the contours and profile of the terrain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, along the line that was drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's have a look at map number 4 now, please. What does that map show?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map represents -- we see the region of Kamenica on our side of the state border, and it shows -- it goes across Junik and shows a point up here to the north of Junik. And underneath that, we have the graph, which shows what is visible. So at the beginning, the green line shows the visibility of one part of the territory and terrain, and visibility on two other places. And all the rest is in red, which means not visible. The distance between these two points is 7.351 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Let's have a look at map number 5 now, please. What line does that show? Is that the line between the Gegaj-Junik area?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is north-west of Gegaj, and the highest elevation point, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. highest point, which is located in this area is in Albania, west of the village of Lukaj. I think it's 1.105 metres altitude, that feature, and it shows the centre of Junik directly. It goes straight to the centre of Junik. And from that point, this is what you can see, or rather, you cannot see anything. There is no visibility line there, no visibility curve at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me be clear about this one. The 3-D picture we've seen is a 3-D view of map number 2? Am I right? Actually, in other words, number 1 picture is a view from this Kodra, Sipsaj - I don't see it - which is 804 point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It corresponds both to map number 2 and map number 3, because they show the same direction, the same axis. So the axis corresponds to both map 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And we're on map 5, which is on the overhead projector, General; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think I've just explained map 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you've just explained map 5, which means that you could only see anything, visibility would only be through the mountains, if you were able to look through mountains?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This has just been done on the basis of relief, not including natural vegetation that exists there on the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So just relief, as if it was bare, a bare terrain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because natural vegetation could make visibility even worse, not to improve it; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Let's take a look at map number 6 now, please, which represents a binocular view and cross-section of the relief of Orahovac-Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a feature above Orahovac, one of the highest points, and it shows the centre of Suva Reka. Only at the very beginning, here, there is slight visibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I must make a point, because time is simply flowing away. None of the selected vantage points is, as far as I know, of any relevance to the evidence of Lord Ashdown. So I'm listening with what I'm prepared to describe as interest to material which it seems to me has no relevance to the case whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Which of these drawings supports your position that Lord Ashdown could not see what he said he saw from where he said he was?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of them. All of them, Mr. Robinson. And the second point, what Mr. Nice has just said, is quite incorrect, because my associates requested that according to Lord Ashdown's testimony as to where he was and what he saw, an exact relief and map be drawn up of what he could see and what he couldn't see. And here you have something, and I invite any expert whom you would like to call to check these images out. The Royal Geographical Society of Great Britain, for instance, anybody. And if they challenge this, then I'll say no more about it. This was a professionally devised set of maps. These are material facts. If he can prove that he can see through a hill, through a mountain, then he was able to see what he saw. But he couldn't have seen what he wrote and what the representatives of the KLA had told him. Had he been with representatives of our own army, then he could have gone and seen what he was interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. How much longer will you spend on this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, because, as you can see, we're moving through these maps very quickly. So this Orahovac-Suva Reka axis, we took the highest feature of Orahovac and were able to see that nothing can be seen, complete invisibility, because there are ten hills to obstruct views.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't that so, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at map number 7, now, please, the Orahovac-Suva Reka axis once again?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above the road between Orahovac and Suva Reka the feature is Gumniste, and the axis is Suva Reka. That's the general direction. There is visibility only in the initial parts for 700 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have a look at number 8 now, please. This feature is Blato, Blato-Suva Reka is the axis. There is visibility just to begin with, in the first part, at this feature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't understand either of the last two. Why do you say in particular in the last one you just can't see anything beyond a few yards? You don't think someone could get into a position where he could see all the way for nine kilometres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, this is topography, which means that we're talking about this axis, this direction, left, right, forward, back, front, behind. If you tell me, I can find what you want to see. I'll find it, the exact point from which you would be able to see what you want to see. However, here, quite obviously, you can see Suva Reka -- you can't. Many directions were used, many axes were used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But looking at your diagram at the bottom, Suva Reka is on the right-hand side at 9. -- is it 9.156 metres? And on the left-hand side, we have the green part that you say is visible. But why can't one see right along the line of the -- the dotted line? What's the obstruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you've just mentioned here is the distance between these two points. Suva Reka is at an altitude of about 400 metres, and this other feature here is at an altitude of 626.6 metres. However, in front of this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... 800. 826.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 826.6. But in front of it, in front of the feature, there's another feature, which blocks the view, blocks visibility towards the whole of Suva Reka. I don't say that at some other point you would not be able to find a feature a little closer, in the region of Dobrodeljane and so on, and then be able to see at least half of Suva Reka, and that would be the south-eastern portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But simply, according to that diagram, there's no obstruction; do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what you think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The obstruction to visibility is at the beginning of the line, straight away. The later ones are not important.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's take a look at map number 10. This is a straight line that has been drawn from one point to link up with another point. However, here, when this relief was done, each point where the land falls off and rises, the rise and fall of the terrain, have been introduced into this graph. And we can see in the first section - this is perhaps 100 metres - then you cannot see a portion. Then you can once again see a portion here, and nothing after that, right up to Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at number 10. General, let's just clarify this. What you've shown here - and these maps are drawn up by experts - they looked at all the possible points and features around Orahovac, from which it was possible to look in this direction?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is north of Orahovac, and certain features were taken, certain elevations were taken, Forsu [phoen], and linked to Suva Reka, at different distances. This point is 14.654 metres away from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have a look at the next one now. What does that show?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, before you proceed, Judge Kwon had put to the witness in relation to map number 8 whether he agreed that there would have been visibility from a particular point, and the witness said: "That's what you think." So I didn't get an explanation from the witness as to whether there would be an obstruction to the view.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I explain this to Mr. Kwon now, please? Mr. Kwon, can you see this? If a person were to be standing at this point here, they would be able to see everything up until this point here. They wouldn't be able to see anything up to this point, but they could see a little portion here. They wouldn't be able to see anything up until this point, and probably this last part, they would be able to see. Now, if they were to move several hundred metres in front. It depends what point you're looking from, the vantage point, if I've made myself clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the next number. We can skip the ones we have commented on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's all similar. Viewed from another feature, called Turine, overlooking Suva Reka, it shows parts that are visible and other parts that are not visible. The distance is 14.654 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is the last map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The last map, where you can also see these peaks.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The visible parts and the invisible parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now put on the overhead projector, please, and comment on the visibility line and the visibility graph. Are there any maps that remain? I gave you yesterday all that I had. I don't have any left.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've shown everything you gave me, and all that remains is the table of visibility and audibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted. It's from the topographic manual. There is a topography manual, Federal Secretariat for Defence, dated 1972, and military topography, General Staff, 1979.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the assistant commander of section manual --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please comment on these subjects of observation. What can you see, at what distance?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is visibility by a naked eye. So a settlement can be seen at a distance of 10 to 12 kilometres. When they say "settlement," they mean populated areas on manoeuvring ground. They're not talking about cities that -- or towns that can be seen at a greater distance as well. A large building can be seen at a distance of eight kilometres. Number 3: A village house, five kilometres. Window on a house, four kilometres. Chimney on top of a roof, three kilometres. A person as a point visible at two kilometres. Tank, distinguishable with difficulty from other combat vehicles, two kilometres. Tank, as distinguished from other combat vehicles, 1.5 kilometres. 9: Tree, pillar, 1.5. 10: Movement of legs in walking, .7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does this table mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is designed to help soldiers know what they can observe at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. various distances so that they can report to their superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you read this supplementary statement by Lord Ashdown yesterday. Did you manage to identify new information now, and what does this information represent?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked last night trying to distil as precise information as possible, and I received the statements provided additionally by Lord Ashdown, mentioning Junik, just as I said before. Shall I show first what I received earlier on, what was provided during Lord Ashdown's testimony, indicating precisely the locations from which he observed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You received that from Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Show it.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was happening in the same courtroom. The pointer is showing Gegaj village. On the back, there is the description of what was seen from that location, what could be seen from that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We see on this photo the pointer of Lord Ashdown as he was using it during his testimony?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. And the second thing I received indicates what Mr. Lord saw from another point, and that other point shows the area of Becej village. I worked with those materials at the time, and they show unequivocally that Lord Ashdown could not see those things. Yesterday I received this supplementary statement, and I worked on it as well. It is very typical that the lord invokes Criminal Code in Bosnia and Herzegovina saying that perjury is prohibited, while everybody knows that the Penal Code of Bosnia and Herzegovina does not bind Lord Ashdown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... comment again. He knows it's inappropriate and I don't know for which audience he's doing it. But the Chamber might like to know that the format of Lord Ashdown's statement is prepared with a view to its being served under provisions of 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'll just tell the witness. Refrain from comments like that, Mr. Delic. You know they are inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While I'm on my feet: The two extracts that the witness has of video footage from Lord Ashdown's evidence were produced in the last hearing involving the witness, but not by us, and I don't actually have, I think, a hard copy of the two photos that he showed, or bits of film that he showed. I'd be grateful if the accused could provide me with a copy, or alternatively, if the witness's copy could be made available to Mr. Nort over the break, and if Mr. Nort might be able to get us a copy. Because I want to be able to deal with what was shown very fleetingly on the overhead projector in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm quite sure Mr. Milosevic will oblige.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, those images, or rather, photographs that the General showed just now were photos received from Mr. Nice during the testimony of that witness, in order to determine precisely what Lord Ashdown was talking about. This witness was asked on the basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In his new statement, Lord Ashdown --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says "private session" on my monitor. Why is it a private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something else was on my monitor a moment ago. It's okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Push the video monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The imagery appeared. I am interested in that image, because I cannot see the map from where I'm sitting, and I want to see it at least on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a map on a scale of 1:50.000. In his statement, the lord provided new coordinates for the locations he was standing at. What I wish to say is the following: If the lord says he was near Gegaj village at a certain point, according to his new coordinates, he was two kilometres away from Gegaj village, on the slopes of the feature Maja Glava, 700 metres or so from the peak of that mountain. Earlier on he was at an altitude of 680 metres, according to his earlier information, he raised it now to 960 metres. So compared to his earlier statement, he increased the altitude by about 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where is that point? Could you mark it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's marked on my map. That point is exactly on the state border, about 700 metres from the feature called Maja Glava, going towards the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it's exactly right on the state border?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lord did not give exact coordinates. The exactitude of my coordinates is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 25 metres, whereas his margin of error is 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I want to be very clear about this. You say that Lord Ashdown, in his recent statement, has given a different coordinate, a coordinate which places him at a higher point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not indicate coordinates. He only indicated Gegaj village. See what the present, the current point is. Two kilometres from Gegaj village and 300 metres higher than the previous altitude he indicated. I just wish to indicate to you the characteristics of that terrain. The border follows the topographical edge. On the Yugoslav side, it falls down rather sharply, and on the Albanian side it sort of falls right into a creek. So just a couple of hundred metres into Albanian territory, you find yourself 300 metres deep in an abyss. So what I'm saying is Lord Ashdown could not have been at this point. As for some other measurements, in order to reach Gegaj from this point, one needs 105 minutes, if you are using topographic manuals, with the proviso that the difference in altitude is 300 metres and with the proviso that you need to cross two kilometres over very inhospitable terrain. The next thing I want to say: In this part of the border belt, around the block house of Morina, there are big chestnut forests, oak forests, and at the point where Lord Ashdown says he was, there are beech forests 100 years old, about 15 metres tall. In this area, there was no clearing of the borderline, and there was no corridor made between two parts -- two sides of the border, which is usually done. I know this because I visited the area several times. Third: At the time that Lord Ashdown invokes, the 23rd -- the month of May and June of that year, and throughout the year, all state authorities were represented 24 hours a day on the border. Only the shifts changed. From the block house of Morina, there is complete control and oversight of the road leading to Kamenica and the Albanian border. From our block house, it is impossible to approach the border without the soldiers manning the block house, the watch-tower, seeing it. There are two state organs represent in this area, in either of these places. A group of 10, 15 men could not have been in the area unnoticed. Another thing: I keep my documents from that time, because my unit was located at the relevant time in the area of Babaj Boks and the area of Duznje, whereas another unit of mine secured Brovina and Molic. A unit from the 125th Brigade secured Ponosevac and another unit from 125th Brigade secured Junik and Batusa. With your leave, I would like to explain why we did that and why those units were present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Pausing there, General. Setting aside the issue whether Lord Ashdown was able to reach the point or not, do you agree that one can see the -- south of Junik from the newly indicated vantage point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have done that too, very precisely.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, I don't know whether you overheard what General Delic said about a dense beech forest being in that area, about 100 years old, 15 metres tall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any man will tell you the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... which is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From that vantage point, it is impossible to see, due to the dense beech forest, it is impossible to see anything south of Junik. Even if we discount the forest, if we take only relief, it's impossible, and I've shown why on a map, or a graph I made. But we need to show it on the overhead projector. This point here is at an altitude of 960 metres, overlooking Molic village, because Lord Ashdown mentioned Molic village. I don't know if you can see on your monitors what I'm showing. We can see that this green part of the line is what Lord Ashdown could see. Later on, after that, he couldn't see anything. So he cannot see Molic village. He cannot see anything up to the asphalt road. He could see what follows: The villages that he indicated later, Njivokaz, Dobros, Berjak and Stuba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we dealing at the border which is near from Gegaj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's this new point. One can see nothing beyond Gegaj. But the lord gave a new vantage point, 300 above the one he indicated earlier. Somebody evidently tried to adjust Lord Ashdown's statement to make it look acceptable and truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That sort of comment won't do from this witness. He's not here to express comments on the Prosecution, and I'm not going to put up with that sort of thing from people like him through the Court, with your leave, he must be restrained and kept in his place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, I've already spoken to you about comments like that. They're inappropriate and they're not acceptable. You are not to make them. Just give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I did this all night. Mr. Nice came yesterday and just brought in a piece of paper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed with your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did my best to do this professionally, and I'm saying in the most professional manner possible, Lord Ashdown could not have seen what he claims to have seen. Brovina, from here, from this point, you can see Brovina. The green colour depicts what can be seen. Red shows what cannot be seen. From an observation point, if we exclude the fact that there are trees there up to 15 metres high, he could see Brovina except for the western group of houses that are right by the hill. Now, the third direction. That is from this point towards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Ponosevac. So from this point, there is visibility, again, I'm saying, if we disregard the forest that is there near the observation point, you can see all the way up to the feature of Planik. Then you cannot see Ponosevac. Or rather, if I'm to be precise, you cannot see Ponosevac to the school. To the south of the school is the farm. This can be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just remind me, Mr. Nice, or someone, did Lord Ashdown give coordinates of his position in his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not in his first evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not in his first evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He explained his position in general terms. He pointed out his position in general terms on the map and he said what he was able to see. And I assume, without having yet had an opportunity to question the witness, which is something I will now in due course be seeking to do on this topic, but I assume that the observation he made about, was it 640 metres altitude or 620 metres altitude, is derived in some way from the placing of the pointer on the map, but I'm not sure. No, he didn't give coordinates to begin with. He pointed the position out and gave it in general terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem about all this evidence is that this point wasn't taken up when it ought to have been taken up, and it just shows the problems that can arise when the accused fails to do -- conduct the case in a professional way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are at the time for the break now, so we'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, on the basis of what you did here now, what you drew, what you marked, does this mean that the drawing you showed actually showed that Lord Ashdown could have seen something only if he had climbed the highest beech tree there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From an observation post only or some high point above the forest. He had to be above the forest. And even then, he could not see the first part of Molic. He could only see Brovina in its entirety, and he could see only the southern part of Ponosevac and the poultry farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But that's only if he had climbed the highest tree there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if he were above the treetops. Let me just mention one more thing. In order to go from that point to the village of Gegaj and go back, three hours are required, according to topographical norms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a short while ago that your security organs at the border were by the border itself and they could see both the border and part of the territory of the Republic of Albania across the border.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1997 and 1998, all the way up to the war, at the border, round the clock there was duty service by the border units. They were reinforced by our units too. And I've already said in this case that my unit secured this area, from Djakovica, Babaj Boks and Duznje, and in depth, the border area up to Morina. The 125th Brigade was in Batusa and Junik, and it secured that area toward Kosare in depth. If somebody saw tanks, every day it was customary at 1000 hours for tanks, APCs, or other self-propelled vehicles to go and be deployed along the road between Junik and Duznje, because that is where the barriers were. They would all have to come to Duznje at 11.00. Once the road would be secured, then the road itself would be opened and everybody would go in his own direction. If there were patients, sick persons from these units, they would be taken towards Djakovica, whereas these people from Djakovica would go for supplies and to see their units. At 3.00 the road would close. Again, the barriers would be placed. The tanks and all these other vehicles would return to their bases, to their units. Smalica [phoen], Njivokaz and this entire area here was held by terrorists, and that's why this had to be done this way. The road was attacked every day. In May, three of my soldiers were killed in the area of Ponosevac and three or four were seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, we have the point. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So bearing in mind this assumed position, was this assumed position under the observation of your security organs at the border?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply, no one could come to that position, because that is the very state border. That is what we call the line itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is actually no man's land.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such thing as no man's land. There is just a rock. On one side it is marked as being ours, and next to it there is a border stone where Albania is marked. So if you just take a single step, you are in Albania. I guess that the lord did not come to our territory to observe our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other part has to do with Suva Reka, the rest of what I did. As for what Mr. Nice gave.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we move on to Suva Reka, Mr. Robinson, in relation to what Mr. Nice claimed, that I did not raise these questions in good time, I consider that to be inappropriate, because I'm using my own time to refute what Mr. Nice considers to be evidence, and that is precisely the right time to do that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me explain to you Mr. Nice's point. It is that you did not seek to contradict the evidence in chief given by Lord Ashdown during cross-examination. That part of his evidence was not challenged. And that is so. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I challenged his evidence, and I could not bring in experts during my cross-examination, or eyewitnesses who could have challenged the details. His testimony about some tanks that were moving down the road and shooting is something that I did challenge. You can read that in the transcript, because I know that that kind of thing did not happen. And now this witness is proving that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're referring to the evidence that specifically relates to what Lord Ashdown said he saw from that point. We're not speaking about other aspects of his evidence. Now please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in terms of Lord Ashdown's testimony, what did you do as far as Suva Reka is concerned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Suva Reka, Lord Ashdown gave some coordinates for the 27th of September, 1998, when he came from Orahovac towards Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The map cannot be seen here at all. I cannot see it at all. Here on the screen, I just have a white rectangle instead of the map. And now nothing. Now I can see the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lord said that he stopped in the area of the village of Studencane and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down when giving numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, the interpreter is asking you to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 34T DM804898 were the coordinates given by Lord Ashdown. I would like to say that the margin of error is 100 metres, whereas I tried to work with a margin of error of 25 metres. According to Lord Ashdown's coordinates, it is this feature here above Studencane. I marked with a little cross here Lord Ashdown's point, although I think that that is elevation 488. After that, Lord Ashdown says: "From that position I saw what I described as Donje Blace, the contour of Donje Blace." It is on 34T DM915954 and 34T DM888968. I found those points referred to by Lord Ashdown. This here is the first one, Cah Duge. It's a curve on the road. The second point is in the area of the village of Blace. However, since there is nothing further written here, these points seem senseless to me in this context. The lord could not have seen these points. If you follow what I'm showing here, right here, it was up to the feature called Grab. And here, up to trig 686, above Semetiste. He could see from here to here, from the point where he was, whereas these two points that he referred to, he could not have seen anything, absolutely -- he could not have seen absolutely anything. I don't know why he's referring to them. Several times I did these calculations, thinking that perhaps I had made a mistake. For me these two points are senseless, and I couldn't work with them further on. I found them and I depicted them on the map. But from the lord's vantage point, they are invisible. That is for the 27th. As for the 28th, Lord Ashdown says: "In relation to the part of my testimony that deals with what I saw near Pecane on the 28th of September, 1998, my assessment is that the coordinates from which I was observing were 34T DM863920." Pecan is the village here. Last time, if you remember, I mentioned that Lord Ashdown was at that feature there, or this one here, when Mr. Milosevic asked me. He could have seen a lot more if he were at any one of these two. Trig 551 is what he refers to now, trig 551. I testified that from that position I saw the villages of Budakovo, which is at 34T DM945891." So here I've found that particular point. It is in one of the areas in the village of Budakovo, near Kokolari Mahala. Then he says that he was observing Macitevo, Gornja Kruscica, and its coordinate is 34T DM944902. So that's Gornja Kruscica. And further on he says that he saw Kruscica as well. Kruscica actually doesn't exist. It is Donja Kruscica. And then the lord said nothing else, in terms of what he saw from there. But he just specified those points. For those particular points, I worked out his visibility line. As for the first two, I didn't work this out because, as I said, it was senseless. So you can see it here for Budakovo. As you can see, the green colour, the green line, denotes what could have been seen. Budakovo can be seen from that vantage point. Of the five areas of the village, the five hamlets, only two were partially visible and the distance of -- between the village and the vantage point was seven and a half to nine and a half kilometres. Because this is a large village, scattered. The next one is the relief for the trig 551, Gornja Kruscica axis. The green line, the green curve, shows what was visible; the red curve, what was invisible. And from the vantage point, you can see most of the Gornja Kruscica village. As far as the village of Donja Kruscica is concerned, you can only see around feature 738. The distance between Gornja Kruscica and this point is eight to nine kilometres metres, and visibility at this village is greatly reduced by the vegetation that exists there. However, looking at it topographically, that village can be seen, largely be seen, at least. And the last one, the last axis mentioned by Lord Ashdown is the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. trig 551 axis and the village of Macitevo, which is located here. And I counted it up to the school building. Up to the school building, which makes it 11.35 kilometres. Once again, the green curve shows visibility, the red curve shows invisibility. From the vantage point, you can see part of the village around the school very well. As I looked -- up to the school. Most of the village which is south-east of the feature, 1270, is completely invisible. You cannot see it at all. And the distance from the village to the front borderline, or back borderline, along the west-east axis is between 11 to 14 kilometres. That means that you can only see part of the village around the school building. And that would be it, on the basis of the coordinates provided by Lord Ashdown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, were you able, and now, having drawn up these maps, can you establish what things that Lord Ashdown said he could see he could actually have seen? Were you able to establish that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are dealing with the period between the 27th and 28th of September, and that is the period when, in that part of the terrain, there was the fifth stage of anti-terrorist struggle going on there. From the distances that I indicated here - and they were the following distances: 8.7 kilometres, 8.25 kilometres, and 11 kilometres - we have to see what can be seen from that distance. Those are the assessments that have to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. According to your assessments, what could be seen?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the statement that I was given, I read out various things. There was an order by the corps command, there was my own order, because I was present myself. I was in the village of Macitevo for two days. And from that distance, counting the visibility, the table of visibility, which I showed you earlier on, that would mean that nothing could be seen of the combat going on, because the distance is far too great. If necessary, I can show you the orders, the order for combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What difference does using binoculars make?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at all events, if you use binoculars, the possibility of seeing something is increased. But one would have to know the characteristics of the binoculars themselves, their range and degree of enlargement, the scale and the lens. But of course, binoculars would help. Whereas what the camera showed, a window, it showed a window, we saw a window, that is quite impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you mentioned an order. Does that order relate to those days, precisely those days when Lord Ashdown, according to his testimony, was in the area?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does refer to those days. But as we were dealing with 1998 and as it was said that 1998 was not relevant, then I do have it, but it wasn't included in the documents provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you show us the order, please, if you have it with you.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the corps decision. May we zoom in on it? It's not very clear. It's the corps decision for action, for that particular action. And this is the corps order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May we know whether these are part of existing documents, whether they are contemporaneous documents, or whether they're documents prepared years later for the VJ Commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic -- or let me ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they are not documents that were subsequently drawn up. These are contemporaneous documents from that time. So this is part of the map. Of course, it wasn't this small. This is a picture of the original map, or part of the map that I received from the corps command. And the title here is [B/C/S spoken] for the 549th Brigade. Whereas this is the order that I received from the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, you have my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The next question that I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... whether this is part of an existing document that's been exhibited or is available in full form, and also, if in due course we're going to be asked to consider whether we should admit these -- accept or challenge the admission of any of these documents, whether the full document is available for our inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's for Mr. Milosevic to say. Mr. Milosevic, is this part of an existing document? Is it part of an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Delic has already explained to us - I'm sure you'll remember - how many exhibits there were and this particular order was not included in the exhibits because it was considered that 1998 was not a relevant year, as you claimed. However, as this question has arisen now, he is showing us that particular order now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So it's not part of an existing document that has been exhibited. Do you have the full document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can ask General Delic that. Does he have the full document?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the document is complete, except for the fact that the maps are small; they're not in the original size and scale. They have been taken with a digital camera and exist in this small scale, whereas the other documents are complete; they're full and complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But those photograph maps exist in the archives, I assume; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what can we see, General?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's always interesting to see witnesses coming for re-examination so well prepared. But if we're going to be shown an extract, may I see both the extract and, in whatever size, the full document? Because I'd like to review it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that may be shown to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, the photo of the full map is not in fact the full map. It may be most of the map. In each case, they're accompanied by orders which of course aren't in translation. I'm not sure how this actually arises by way of re-examination, if the exercise currently being performed is re-examination as opposed to some other exercise. But I would be grateful, please, for provision of copies of these documents by some system if they're going to be relied on at all by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, as long as we don't say otherwise, it is re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, yes. But it seems to me the scope of this re-examination is almost unprecedented. But there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Let us proceed quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very quickly, Mr. Robinson. But let me just respond to the question raised by Mr. Nice. The witness knew about the problem of maps and that we did not complete our re-examination concerning the maps shown by Lord Ashdown. So bearing in mind the maps, his testimony, and the days which he mentions in his testimony, quite logically he brought with him and brought the documentation, in case it should prove necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, would you please be so kind as to tell us, but just briefly, as was suggested by Mr. Robinson, something with respect to the order you showed us. What's characteristic about that particular order? You have the corps order there, you have your own order. What's all that about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that it was the fifth stage of anti-terrorist actions. The order was given on the 25th of September, 1998. It was the last territory of Kosovo and Metohija, if I can put it that way, where there were still groups of terrorist forces which had not been routed and demilitarised. At the beginning, it says that on the border territory of the mountains Jezero, Siptar forces, sabotage forces, were deployed. Their strength was about 1.700 men to 2.200 terrorists, and they were grouped in detachments, battalions and organised in the following manner for combat. And then we have listed the regions in which they were located and how many men there were in each region. It says here the Sopina axis, Vuka-Macija axis, there were approximately 300 to 400 Siptar terrorists in that locality, and they were deployed in the villages in groups of 20 terrorists, 20 terrorists in the villages, and they were also deployed in houses and schools. The staff command was in Burzaja. Along the axis of Recani the village of Krustica Budakovo, there were about 500 Siptar terrorists grouped in the villages in groups of 25 terrorists, accommodated in the houses. The staff command is in the village of Budakovo. And within the composition of that group, there were also 20 Mujahedin. In the TT 738 region, there was a small group of terrorists, which so far was active. Along the Budakovo-Kruscica road, that's the next point. And Budakovo-Gornja Kruscica, there were mines that were activated by remote control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Let's just stop there in order to save time. The material time, the time that we're discussing, that was a legitimate anti-terrorist operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the last anti-terrorist operation to have been undertaken on the basis of that plan, which had five stages. After this particular operation, once that was completed, the verifiers arrived and different activities ensued, quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let's move on now to another area. General, Mr. Nice, during the cross-examination, on several occasions, asked you about the measures of responsibility towards offices. I would like to ask you to place this document on the overhead projector. I have it here. It is dated the 17th of April, 1999. Is it a document which speaks about the measure of responsibility and liability.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Milosevic explain what he means by measure of responsibility of offices, translated literally.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a very brief document. Could you just take a look at the document and tell us whether that is indeed one of the documents which speaks about that topic, the measures of accountability or responsibility.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The copy is not a clear one, but this is a document which informs the commanders and officers of the units that one brigade commander was dismissed, was replaced, and that an investigation was underway and measures for prosecution had been undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, General. You certainly had occasion to read - or maybe you didn't; I'll give you a copy to be placed on the overhead projector - a copy of the letter of the main staff of the KLA, addressed to the commander of the NATO force, Wesley Clark. In the English original, it is number 00812264. And I will give you the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. translation into Serbian. Could you please give the witness the Serbian version and place the English on the original [as interpreted]. Since I have only that copy, could you please read the first paragraph, and then we will try to cover at least some major points. What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date says Kosovo, 18th of April, 1999, Main Staff of the KLA. This letter is addressed to Mr. Wesley Clark, the commander of the NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that is still the first month of the NATO aggression against Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first paragraph: "Please accept our thanks in the name of all soldiers and officers --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Stop. Mr. Milosevic, I'm not going to allow you to read this letter in its entirety. If there are particular areas that you wish to focus on, then do so. We don't have the time to read the entire letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Apart from the expression of gratitude, is there any reference in the letter to certain activities that the NATO forces should concentrate on in the view of the commander of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is interesting. "We are working on opening a land corridor, because on the other side of the border - they mean Albania - there is a large number of volunteers." That is an interesting point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It also mentions the locations of our forces. It says that they should be targeted. Is all that written in this letter?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, the last paragraph: "We know that your air force was guided by the motto do not strike bees; strike their nests. But to Serbia, except for their aviation, which nest you have completely destroyed, the other nests, that is, tank units, artillery units, motorised infantry units, et cetera, have been moved out of their nests and dispersed. The damage that you are doing to Serbia's economic and military potential will force it to capitulate, but it needs time, which for the KLA is painful. We think that at the time that when the Serb army is dispersed, because they have knowledge of the fact of delay of your ground troops, Serbia has spread its forces, but at the moment it is not coordinated, not led or guided well, and incapable of replying quickly and effectively to your ground forces." There is another reference to manoeuvres of Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I see that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let it be passed to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I don't know if the accused would be good enough to -- just one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not sure now that arose incidentally out of cross-examination, but it may be I missed the point. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is without doubt a document of the other side, and its number was 00812264. It is a document which indubitably proves coordinated action between the KLA and the NATO forces, and I would like it exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: First of all, Your Honours, is this re-examination or is this additional evidence, A? B, if I'd been given advance notice of this document, I'd know whether I had any position to take on it. At the moment I'm just investigating what our position on the document may be. The fact that it's served may or may not reflect acceptance of it as genuine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber will admit the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think it had a respectable origin in our hands. I've been able to trace that much. But it really is very difficult to deal with material coming in this way without any advance notice, whether it's relevant in re-examination or not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you're embarrassed in any way, Mr. Nice, you can ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on those photographs from the book titled "Genocide Against Serbs Towards the End of the Nineteenth Century" and could you tell us what they represent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How does that arise, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is obviously about the training of KLA members in the neighbouring Albania from which both NATO and the Albanian state acted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not allowing this in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Let me ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, was Malisevo within your zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Malisevo was covered by my peacetime area of responsibility, and in the maps shown here, that was also indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When was the last time you were in Malisevo yourself?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to pass through rather often, but the last time I was there in April 1999, the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Although I have never been there myself, I know it is a very small place. What was the importance of such a small place, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
